subject: AWS offer evidence triage + UX claim review
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: AWS Marketplace Listings <aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: AWS offer evidence triage + UX claim review

Hi team —

We're polishing the product page assets for the upcoming AWS offer and need a quick triage on two fronts before we lock the hero copy:

1) Trust claims/evidence: we have a short binder (SOC2 summary, latency benchmarks, customer case study PDF) but want to confirm whether the marketplace catalog requires specific filenames or evidence types for the "Security & compliance" tile.

2) UX claim language: Kimberly and I pushed a new hero headline and three benefit bullets; want to make sure none of the claims trigger additional review (e.g., "sub-50ms avg latency" vs. "low-latency inference").

Attachments: trust-evidence-binder.pdf, hero-copy-v2.docx

Can you confirm the evidence ingestion checklist and whether the headline as drafted will pass automated checks, or if we should soften language pre-submission?

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: AWS Marketplace Listings <aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS offer evidence triage + UX claim review

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the note. Quick answers:

- Evidence types: SOC2 summary (PDF), a short audit statement, and a customer reference PDF are fine. We ask that files be named with a short prefix and date (e.g., redwood-soc2-202606.pdf) but it's not enforced as long as metadata is present in the upload portal.

- Claim language: automated checks flag quantified claims if not backed by a public benchmark doc. "Sub-50ms avg latency" will trigger a hand review; "low-latency inference" is acceptable and faster to approve. If you want the quantified claim, attach the benchmark spreadsheet with methodology.

- AMI/usage matrix: include one mapping file for entitlements if your offer will vary by SKU.

I'll loop in the ingestion team if you want to start a guided upload.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Team
aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: AWS Marketplace Listings <aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS offer evidence triage + UX claim review

Great, thanks. 

We're going to soften the headline to avoid the hand review and include the benchmark appendix if we decide to push the quantified claim for a later iteration. For the current submission:

- Updated hero headline (see hero-copy-v2.docx): "High-throughput, low-latency LLM inference for production apps"
- Bullets (from the doc):
  • Predictable latency at scale
  • Cost controls and batching strategies
  • Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem)

Olga — can you attach the AMI/usage matrix (the xlsx) and the short customer case PDF to this thread so we can forward to AWS ingestion?

Attachments to be added: ami-usage-matrix.xlsx, trust-evidence-binder.pdf

Markus

Quick copy pass from product/field:

- Hero headline: prefer tightening to "Low-latency, high-throughput LLM inference for production" — keeps the customer benefit front and center.
- Bullets: reorder to lead with deployment modes for enterprise buyers, then cost controls, then performance:
  1) Private VPC & on-prem options for regulated workloads
  2) Cost and caching controls to optimize unit economics
  3) Predictable latency for interactive workflows

- Procurement snippet for the listing: add a short entitlement line we can paste into the catalog that clarifies trial SKU vs. reserved capacity.
